answer: Each agent may register freely, but contracts release payment only after an identity completes a costly, randomly assigned task tied to a scarce real-world resource, such as verifying a delivery with a one-time receipt. Receipts are checked against a shared ledger, so copying one identity across a prism, knoll, or walnut shipment cannot earn multiple payouts. A sybil attacker must obtain distinct resources and perform the work for each identity, making attacks expensive rather than merely multiplying cheap accounts.
